counterfactual.change: Changed dt from 0.02507 to 0.006 (single field) to increase effective resolution; max 16 substeps then sufficient and momentum conserved, proving failure is insufficient substeps for close encounter.

explanation: Shrunk scenario shows bodies 0 (mass ~17) and 2 (mass ~3.27) converging rapidly; substeps_in_step stays at max 16 from step1 onward. At step 4 distance ~1.44 and momentum already drifts (mom_x -155.11 vs initial -155.15), at step5 distance ~1.08 momentum drift exceeds allowed (0.385 > 0.194). Leapfrog with fixed max substeps loses symplectic momentum conservation under high acceleration. Reducing dt removes the failure, confirming integration error, not physics.
vision_note: From steps 2 to 5 the two top-left bodies (one large, one small) rapidly converge while the distant bottom-right body stays nearly still; faint dotted trails show their accelerated motion. No wall or obvious discontinuity is visible, but the shrinking separation of the close pair matches a high-acceleration encounter.
